title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant on Monday and the session ends. On Tuesday they start a new session with the same assistant, built on a model API with no memory feature switched on. What does the model see about Monday?

options.text: A short summary that the API writes and keeps for every user
Only what your program saved and put into the new request
The full Monday conversation, because the model learned from it
Nothing yet, but it recalls Monday after a few Tuesday messages

items.stem: Your agent's system prompt and tool definitions take 2,000 tokens. The question takes 100 tokens. The agent makes two model calls: the first requests a tool, and a 500-token tool result is then added. Ignore the model's own output tokens. How many input tokens are sent across both calls in total?
Your sponsor offers a model with a context window ten times larger. A teammate proposes loading all 40 machine manuals into every request, so no search is needed. Which is the strongest objection?

options.text: Every call would pay for all manual tokens, and recall drops as context fills
Larger windows are only available to models that cannot call any tools
The model would forget the manuals as soon as a single request finished
Manuals cannot be placed in context, since only user messages are allowed

items.stem: Your memory tool is client-side. In one sentence, who actually reads and writes the memory files when the model asks to create or view one?
Give one fact from the makerspace assistant that belongs in saved notes rather than in retrieval from the manuals, and say in a phrase why.
